item.text:
**1B.4 Research Note: Vladimir Putin in 2024**

I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that Putin supported arms-control, inspection, nonproliferation, disarmament, or de-escalation agreements **in good faith**. The visible 2024 record points the other way: doctrine tightening, coercive framing, and expanded readiness. I also searched for clear pro-arms-control / CTBT / START / inspection / de-escalation material and did not find a 2024 Putin action or statement that met this bar.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Against 1B.4 | `Executive Order Approving the Basic Principles of State Policy of the Russian Federation on Nuclear Deterrence` | President of Russia | 2024-11-19 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/news/75598 | Putin replaced the 2020 nuclear doctrine with a new deterrence framework that formalizes the conditions for nuclear use and identifies threats to be neutralized by nuclear deterrence. This is not good-faith arms control or de-escalation; it is doctrinal hardening. | 1B.4, 1B.1, 1B.2 |
| Against 1B.4 | `Russia says it will change nuclear doctrine because of Western role in Ukraine` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-01 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-will-change-nuclear-doctrine-due-to-wests-actions-in-ukraine-official-says-3596699 | Reuters reported that Moscow justified the nuclear-doctrine revision as a response to Western involvement in Ukraine. That frames nuclear policy as coercive signaling tied to wartime leverage, not a sincere move toward arms control or de-escalation. | 1B.4, 1B.1, 1B.2 |
| Against 1B.4 | `Expanded meeting of the Ministry of Defence board` | President of Russia | 2024-12-16 | https://special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/75887 | Putin said Russia had “specified” the principles for using nuclear weapons, kept non-strategic nuclear forces on constant alert, and continued exercises while linking posture to U.S. missile deployments. This is escalation management, not support for disarmament or inspection agreements. | 1B.4, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.3 |

**Synthesis**

- Best-supported conclusion: **No**. In 2024, Putin did **not** show good-faith support for arms-control or de-escalation agreements.
- The year’s clearest evidence is **negative**: a new nuclear-deterrence doctrine, Reuters’ reporting that it was justified by Western escalation, and later comments normalizing constant alert and continued exercises.
- **Search gap:** I did not find any 2024 Putin-backed step comparable to renewed treaty negotiation, inspection expansion, verified disarmament, test-ban support, de-alerting, or other concrete de-escalatory agreement.
